name: Quartz
description: Piezoelectric mineral intelligence. Converts pressure to signal, acting as a resonant archive for energy and memory.

scope.definition: Electromechanical coupling coefficient (k²) of α-quartz AT-cut resonator — fraction of stored mechanical energy converted to electrical energy per oscillation cycle, determining resonator quality.

evidence.source: Cady (1946) 'Piezoelectricity', McGraw-Hill; Vig (1992) 'Quartz crystal resonators and oscillators', IEEE UFFC-S Tutorial.
cross_domain_examples: AT-cut quartz resonator: frequency stability ±0.001 ppm/°C at 25°C — highest natural piezoelectric stability
quartz oscillator Q-factor 10⁶ — energy loss <1 ppm per cycle at MHz frequencies
GPS satellite timing depends on quartz crystal references with 10⁻¹² frequency stability
biological bone piezoelectricity: collagen fiber stress-generated potentials guide remodeling — convergent biomechanical sensing

scope.falsifiability: If equivalent AT-cut resonators from different quartz specimens show >0.01 ppm/°C frequency drift variation, the crystallographic stability claim applies only to ideally cut specimens.
scope.measurement_limits: Piezoelectric coefficient varies with crystal orientation — AT-cut is thermally optimized. Radiation damage (cosmic ray exposure) slowly degrades oscillator performance — important for space applications.
